as_told.title: SRI remote viewing tests and Ingo Swann

plain: Starting in the 1970s, the CIA (the US foreign intelligence agency) ran a psychic spy program built on remote viewing, the claimed ability to describe distant places using only the mind. According to Michels, the scientist Hal Puthoff ran that program. Michels says many of its remote viewers reported seeing beings in different places, and that one viewer, Ingo Swann, saw them on the far side of the Moon. He also names another viewer, Joe McMoneagle. The researcher Peter Levenda, without naming a source, puts the weight somewhere else: the tests at SRI, the California research institute where the work was done, showed statistical improvements in results, and Swann did what Levenda calls tremendous work there.
